highlights.summary: Compares imipridone drugs in prostate cancer models that no longer depend on androgens, and positions ONC212 as the lead candidate using phenotypic and transcriptomic profiling.
Low-intensity focused ultrasound, delivered through the skull, increases the birth of new neurons in the hippocampus through BDNF signaling.
The imipridone ONC206 acts against colorectal cancer stem/progenitor cells, both in 3D cultures and in patient-derived organoids.
A urinary tract infection, far from the brain, is enough to suppress the birth of new neurons in the adult hippocampus.
Establishes and characterizes prostate organoids from patients who had not yet received any treatment.
Tideglusib, a GSK-3β inhibitor, curbs the growth of neuroblastoma stem/progenitor cells in culture and in animals.
A step-by-step protocol for enriching prostate cancer stem/progenitor cells by growing them as three-dimensional spheres.
Stimulating the thalamus in awake rats triggers the birth of new neurons in the hippocampal formation.
An extract of Berberis libanotica, a barberry native to Lebanon, shows anticancer effects on prostate cancer stem/progenitor cells.
